content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Design a geometric model consisting of two square plates, each with an edge length of 140mm and a thickness of 10mm. Position these plates so that they intersect at a 90-degree angle, creating an L-shape configuration. On one of these plates, incorporate a square cutout measuring 45x45mm. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation strategy (function-call only):

1. Horizontal plate  
   • Use functions.block to create the first solid.  
   • Dimensions: x_size = 140, y_size = 140, z_size = 10 (lying flat in the XY-plane, 10 mm thick upward in +Z).  
   • Base-point: x = 0, y = 0, z = 0.  
   • subtraction = False (this establishes the initial geometry).

2. Vertical plate (forming the 90-degree “L”)  
   • Add a second block with the same square face but turned upright by letting its thickness lie along the X-axis.  
   • Dimensions: x_size = 10 (thickness), y_size = 140, z_size = 140.  
   • Base-point: x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 so that it shares the lower-left edge with the horizontal plate and the two plates intersect through the first 10 mm of height, giving the desired right-angle connection.  
   • subtraction = False (this is added material).

3. Square cut-out in the horizontal plate  
   • Subtract a third block.  
   • Dimensions: x_size = 45, y_size = 45, z_size = 10 (cuts completely through the 10-mm thickness).  
   • Base-point: x = 47.5, y = 47.5, z = 0 (centers the opening in the 140 × 140 plate).  
   • subtraction = True.

Parameter arrays for one single functions.block call:  
x_size = [140, 10, 45]  
y_size = [140, 140, 45]  
z_size = [10, 140, 10]  
x      = [0, 0, 47.5]  
y      = [0, 0, 47.5]  
z      = [0, 0, 0]  
subtraction = [False, False, True]

Once you ask me to “prepare the function call,” I will supply the exact functions.block invocation with those arrays.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
